name: Udemy, Inc.

profile.description: Udemy operated a global online learning marketplace with over 250,000 courses across technology, business, and personal development, serving 85 million learners. The platform offered Udemy Business, a subscription-based enterprise solution representing 72% of revenue. Udemy was acquired by Coursera (COUR) on May 11, 2026, and delisted from NASDAQ. The combined entity is valued at ~$2.5B.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Udemy successfully pivoted from a consumer-first marketplace to an enterprise-focused subscription platform — subscription revenue reached $566M (72% of total) growing 8% YoY, and paid consumer subscribers grew 102% YoY to 343,000 [1]. However, total revenue was essentially flat at $789.8M (+0.4% YoY) as the consumer segment declined 9%, reflecting cannibalization rather than expansion. AI Deployment (1/2): Udemy launched an AI Assistant with natural-language chat and skills-mapping features, offered AI transformation packages to enterprise customers, and expanded leadership with three AI-focused hires from Airbnb and YouTube in June 2025 [2]. No specific AI revenue or cost savings quantified. Market Share (1/2): 85M learners and 250K+ courses make Udemy a major online learning platform, but the Coursera merger acknowledged neither platform alone commanded market leadership [3]. Pipeline (0/2): Company was acquired by Coursera on May 11, 2026, eliminating independent product roadmap and forward guidance [3]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No specific R&D spending data available to assess relative to industry peers.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Udemy's mission to 'transform lives through learning' is clear and purposeful, connecting the business to democratizing education globally. However, accepting a below-IPO acquisition price raises questions about whether the mission sustained strategic conviction or whether financial pressures ultimately prevailed [4]. Community Impact (0/2): Serving 85M learners and enabling 75,000+ instructors to earn income teaching is the business model itself, not separate philanthropy. No foundation, quantified charitable programs, or community investment identified. Employee Retention (0/2): Two rounds of layoffs — 10% in 2023 and 20% (280 employees) in 2024 — with offshoring of roles. Post-merger Coursera layoffs added further instability with $8-11M in severance costs [5]. Insider Buying (0/2): CEO Hugo Sarrazin purchased $257K in shares in May 2025, but this was followed by 47 insider sales vs. 2 buys over the trailing year and ultimate sale of the company at a steep discount to IPO price [6].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanical calculation: D/E 4.9% well below 70% target (score 1.0, 1x); ROE 1.9% below 15% target (score 0.13, 2x); Revenue Growth YoY 0.4% below 10% target (score 0.68, 1x); Revenue Growth 5yr CAGR ~13% above 10% target (score 1.0, 2x); Forward P/E 8.41 well below 20 target (score 1.0, 1x); Profit Margin 0.48% below 20% target (score 0.02, 1x); PEG unavailable, excluded. Weighted sum = 4.95, max = 8, score = round(6.2) = 6 [7]. Balance sheet was nearly debt-free ($10.2M total debt, $210.5M equity) with $359M in cash. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 700bps to 12% ($95.3M) in FY2025, and free cash flow reached $78.5M [1]. Liquidity floor cleared: 2.37M avg volume x $4.63 = $11.0M.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (4/9 — EXPOSED): Udemy's core product — pre-recorded video courses from independent instructors — faces meaningful AI substitution risk. Free AI tutors from ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Khan Academy's Khanmigo provide personalized, interactive instruction that competes directly with static video content [2]. The consumer segment's 9% YoY decline may already reflect this competitive pressure. The marketplace model risks disintermediation as AI generates increasingly high-quality educational content at near-zero marginal cost. However, Udemy Business enterprise subscriptions (72% of revenue) have higher switching costs, compliance requirements, and credential needs that AI cannot easily replicate [1]. AI Opportunity (1/1): Udemy generates AI-related revenue through AI skills training courses (among the highest-demand categories), AI transformation packages for enterprises, and the AI Assistant that enhances learner engagement [2].

infinite_game.summary: Udemy exhibited some infinite-game qualities in its mission to democratize education, but the company's trajectory — two major layoff rounds, offshoring, consumer segment decline, and ultimate sale to Coursera at a steep discount to IPO price — paints a picture of a company that struggled to sustain independent viability rather than one built to endure [3][5].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): 'Transform lives through learning' is a genuine cause bigger than the company — connecting the platform's work to democratizing global education [4]. The 85M-learner reach and 75K+ instructor ecosystem demonstrate partial execution. However, the willingness to sell to Coursera at a significant discount to IPO price, after multiple restructurings, suggests the cause did not ultimately sustain the strategic conviction needed to play the infinite game independently.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Two layoff rounds in 18 months (10% in 2023, 20% in 2024) with offshoring of eliminated roles to lower-cost locations fundamentally undermined employee trust [5]. Post-merger, Coursera announced additional layoffs with $8-11M in severance costs. CEO turnover (three CEOs in 5 years as a public company) adds organizational instability. This is a textbook low-trust environment by Sinek's standard.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): The Coursera merger is the definitive acknowledgment of a worthy rival — Udemy recognized Coursera's credential strength as complementary to its own broad skills marketplace, framing the combination as better serving learners rather than defeating a competitor [3]. Management explicitly cited 'complementary offerings' in the merger rationale, showing infinite competitive mindset.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Udemy evolved from a consumer-only marketplace to an enterprise-focused subscription platform, with Udemy Business growing to 72% of revenue [1]. The consumer subscription model (subscribers up 102% YoY) represents a meaningful business model shift from transactional purchases. However, accepting the Coursera acquisition represents capitulation more than bold strategic reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): The enterprise pivot required investing in a new go-to-market motion while accepting consumer revenue decline — a meaningful short-term sacrifice for long-term recurring revenue quality [1]. CEO Sarrazin purchased $257K in shares shortly after joining, showing personal conviction [6]. However, the layoff-and-offshore restructuring is a cost-optimization playbook, and accepting a below-IPO acquisition suggests limited appetite for the harder path of independent scale.

investment_thesis: Udemy was acquired by Coursera on May 11, 2026, creating the world's most comprehensive skills platform with 180M+ combined learners. The final-year FY2025 results showed improving profitability — adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 700bps to 12% ($95.3M), subscription revenue grew 8% to $566M (72% of total), and paid consumer subscribers surged 102% to 343,000 [1]. The enterprise business (ARR $540M) demonstrated durable demand for corporate upskilling. The Inspire Impact Score of 58 (ALIGNED) reflects positive contributions across 13 ESG dimensions including product access, customer welfare, and data security.
thesis_continued: As a completed acquisition, the investment case is now moot for new positions. The bear case that materialized: total revenue was essentially flat (+0.4% YoY) as the consumer segment declined 9%, and the company accepted Coursera's ~$930M all-stock offer at a steep discount to its $4B+ IPO market cap [3]. AI disruption was the structural threat — free AI tutors threatened to commoditize pre-recorded video instruction, the core product [2]. Two layoff rounds (30% cumulative reduction) and three CEOs in 5 years as a public company reflect the operational challenges of competing independently in online learning. Post-merger, Coursera is already cutting jobs with $8-11M in severance costs [5].
key_catalysts: Combined Coursera-Udemy platform positions the merged entity as the dominant global online learning platform with 180M+ learners and both credential and broad skills capabilities [3]
Enterprise subscription ARR of $540M (+4% YoY) with expanding EBITDA margins provides stable recurring revenue base for the combined entity [1]
AI skills training courses are among the highest-demand categories, positioning the platform to benefit from the corporate AI upskilling wave across all industries [2]
key_risks: AI disruption — free AI tutors from OpenAI, Google, and Khan Academy threaten to commoditize pre-recorded video instruction; consumer segment already declining 9% YoY [2]

Post-merger integration risk — combining two historically unprofitable edtech platforms (combined ~2,700 employees) with overlapping functions and different cultures; Coursera already announcing layoffs [5]
Revenue stagnation — total revenue was essentially flat (+0.4%) in FY2025 as consumer decline offset enterprise growth; unclear whether the merged entity can re-accelerate top-line growth [1]
